reviewer_lane: fresh source-only independent review; zero authorship
scope: Review only the source commit and current source/tests. No native browser proof, build, release, DB, inventory, or product changes.

verdict_a.finding: The source now distinguishes the expected missing, empty, other chrome-extension origin, and non-extension documentUrl cases. It performs one additional bounded-by-attempt-count observation after the exact context check fails, so a subsequent exact owned-worker context is visible as a transient registration window. The original requireSidePanelContext predicate remains contextType SIDE_PANEL plus exact expected documentUrl plus tabId -1; foreign/unowned contexts cannot satisfy it.

verdict_a.limit: No native run was performed in this lane. This verifies the diagnostic's ability to distinguish these cases when observed; it does not establish what Chrome returned on the failing run or prove the root cause.

verdict_b.finding: Reuse is good: the diagnostic delegates to the existing observeSidePanelContext helper, avoids raw URLs and exception text, preserves the acceptance guard, and tests distinguish initial classification, exact later appearance, persistent mismatch, and query error. Existing foreign-context refusal coverage remains present. The follow-up is limited to two observer attempts, but neither readContexts nor waitBetween has a wall-clock deadline here; a stalled CDP request can hold the original failure path indefinitely. The followUpQueryFailed flag also reports any observer exception, not strictly a query failure.
